newsitem.title: USA: Rains seen returning to U.S. Midwest on Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Rains seen returning to U.S. Midwest on Tuesday.

text.p: Corn and soybean harvest in the U.S. Midwest will likely be slowed again this week as a rain system moves across the area Tuesday, meteorologists said.

"Tomorrow, we should see a rapid increase in cloudiness and there will be rain, probably during the morning," said Joel Burgio, meteorologist with Weather Services Corp. "The rainiest weather will be in west sections of the (corn) belt."
He forecast rainfall amounts of 0.30 to 1.50 inches with general coverage in the western Corn Belt. The eastern belt can expect rainfall amounts 0.10 to 0.50 inches, he said.

Temperatures should remain normal to above normal through Wednesday but a cold front was expected to move southward by Thursday, dropping temperatures below to much below normal, said Tim Bowden, meteorologist with Weather Express.
"Once the front goes through, high temperatures will fall from the 60s (degrees Farenheit) to the 40s and lows from the 40s to 20s," he said.
Snow was likely in the northwest extremes of the belt Thursday and Friday but only flurries were forecast for the central portion. The eastern Corn Belt should see light showers, Bowden said.

Long-range forecasts indicated a slight warm-up on Saturday but increasing cloudiness, Burgio said. Light to moderate showers were expected Saturday night and Sunday with a few sprinkles lingering on Monday, he said.
